subject.title: [Feature]: Script to restore session history archived by new daily-reset mechanism (introduced v2026.2+)

question: Should OpenClaw solve reset archive recovery through read-only family history only, a doctor-owned restore/re-index command, or both?
rationale: The choice changes public API shape, model-facing access to archived sensitive transcripts, and whether OpenClaw mutates archived session files, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
options.body: Use the bounded `includeFamily` style path as the supported retrieval mechanism before adding any archive-mutating command.

options.title: Add Doctor Restore/Re-Index
options.body: Provide a deliberate recovery command for already affected users that preserves source metadata and explains retention and security consequences.

options.title: Reject Mutation Restore
options.body: Keep archive recovery read-only and track any reset-policy or warning work separately.

recommendation.title: Land Read-Only Family History First
recommendation.body: Use the bounded `includeFamily` style path as the supported retrieval mechanism before adding any archive-mutating command.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main and release-history routing candidate for the active reset archive fallback and related session-history surface.
